info.name: Invictus AI Agents
info.description:
API collection for the Invictus AI Agents platform.

**Setup:** Start Docker services, API server, and Celery worker before running requests.

**Auth:** All authenticated endpoints require a JWT Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

**Run lifecycle:** Runs are async. After triggering a run (202), poll `GET /runs/{run_id}` for state. Valid `status` values are `queued`, `running`, `complete`, `failed`, `cancelled`. (HITL was removed on 2026-05-06 — there are no longer `awaiting_review` / `resuming` states or any `/runs/{id}/resume` endpoint.)

**MCP behavior:**
- `enabled_mcps` is **strict opt-in** — omitting it (or sending `[]`) means **no MCP tools**. Pass an explicit list (e.g. `["engage", "plan", "insights"]`) to enable modules.
- Active modules: `engage` (21 tools), `plan` (14), `insights` (9). Stub modules `client-portal` and `deals` are **silently dropped** even if listed — their tools are not registered.
- `FORBIDDEN` errors from an MCP server are **sticky for the run**: the offending server is removed from the toolset, and subsequent iterations don't see its tools.
- `partial: true` envelopes from fan-out tools are surfaced (Copilot prepends a `[Partial result: ...]` annotation). Never retry partials.

**Folder structure:**
- **Infrastructure** — Health checks, discovery, error cases, LLM security
- **Sample Workflows** — Proof-of-concept workflows (echo, doc_research, web_search, calculator)
- **Workflows** — Production business workflows (Client 360, Copilot, Daily Briefing legacy, Unified Run, Quality Feedback)

item.name: Sample Workflows
item.description:
Proof-of-concept workflows for testing platform capabilities. These demonstrate how the agent framework works — triggering runs, polling status, RAG integration, and tool calling.

Not intended for production use. See the **Workflows** folder for business workflows.

item.name: Echo
item.description: Basic echo workflow — completes immediately. Useful for smoke-testing auth, the run lifecycle, and llm_config plumbing. Includes llm_config with Anthropic Claude Haiku.

item.name: Document Research
item.description:
Document research workflow — extracts fields and analyses documents via RAG Gateway.

Requires:
- RAG Gateway running (RAG_GATEWAY_URL in .env)
- Celery worker running
- Documents indexed in RAG Gateway

item.name: Web Search
item.description:
Web search workflow — searches the web using Tavily and returns structured results with a summary.

Requires:
- TAVILY_API_KEY set in .env
- Celery worker running

item.name: Calculator
item.description:
Financial calculator workflow — computes MOIC, TVPI, IRR, and compound growth from PE fund data.

No external dependencies required — all calculations are pure math.

item.name: LLM Provider Examples
item.description:
Examples of triggering workflows with different LLM providers and models.

Each request demonstrates how to pass `llm_config` to select a specific provider and model. The echo workflow is used for simplicity — the same `llm_config` pattern works with any workflow.

item.name: Client 360
item.description:
Advisor-scoped Client 360 / Daily Briefing — the production morning briefing workflow.

**Pipeline (6 phases):**
1. `discover_clients` — calls `engage_list_my_clients` with the advisor's JWT to enumerate clients.
2. `process_clients_fanout` — per-client deep dive against Engage / Plan / Insights, with a 3-hour PostgreSQL cache (advisor-agnostic) so a client touched by another advisor is reused.
3. `run_macro_news` — single consolidated cross-client news search; articles are tagged with `affected_clients`.
4. `fetch_calendar` — pulls upcoming events for meeting briefs.
5. `generate_advisor_aggregations` — rollup: portfolio summary, segmentation, deployment gaps, top alerts, top news, meeting briefs.
6. `generate_run_summary` — final markdown narrative.

**Authentication contract — credentials live in headers, body is for data:**
- `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` (required) — 30-min JWT issued at `POST {auth_backend}/api/v1/auth/login`. Decoded by FastAPI for routing/auth and forwarded to every MCP server.
- `X-Refresh-Token: <refresh_token>` (optional but **strongly recommended**) — 60-min refresh JWT from the same login response. When present, the workflow's `TokenManager` rotates the access token mid-run (proactively when < 5 min remain, reactively on a single `AUTH_FAILURE`). Without it, a long fan-out hits upstream auth failures once the 30-min access TTL elapses (root cause of the 2026-05-09 empty-briefing trace).
- Body: `{ "llm_config": ... }` — no credentials.

Login once, paste the two raw JWTs into the `access_token` and `refresh_token` collection variables; the trigger request reads from `{{auth_token}}` (= `Bearer {{access_token}}`) and `{{refresh_token}}`.

**Modules required:** `engage`, `plan`, `insights` (all three MCP servers must be reachable).

**Output:** `{ discovery, clients, macro_news, calendar_events, advisor_summary, data_discrepancies, run_summary }`. Per-client briefings carry `data_gaps` (real failures) and `partial_data_notes` (documented expected upstream partials such as `documents` POST-not-supported or `transfers` 404).

header.description: Optional. Refresh JWT (60-min TTL) issued at /auth/login. When present, the Client 360 workflow rotates the access token mid-run instead of failing on expiry. Leave blank to opt out.

request.description:
Trigger the production Client 360 / Daily Briefing run.

**Headers:**
- `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` — required. Authenticates the API call and is forwarded to every Engage / Plan / Insights MCP server. Sourced from `{{auth_token}}` which expands to `Bearer {{access_token}}`.
- `X-Refresh-Token: <refresh_token>` — optional but recommended. Lets the workflow's `TokenManager` rotate the access token mid-run (proactively when < 5 min remain, reactively on a single `AUTH_FAILURE`). Without it, runs longer than the 30-min access-token TTL will hit upstream auth failures partway through. Sourced from `{{refresh_token}}`.

**Body:**
- `llm_config` — optional model override. The body carries no credentials; tokens always travel in headers.

Saves run_id to the collection variable for use in the next request.

**Note:** This run is long — fan-out per client + macro news + calendar + summary. Expect 30s–5min depending on client count and cache hits. With `X-Refresh-Token` set, runs longer than 25 min still complete cleanly because the token gets rotated automatically.

item.name: Unified Run Endpoint
item.description:
Unified run endpoint — POST /agents/run.

Single entry point for all workflows. Accepts an optional `workflow` field — if omitted, an LLM router auto-classifies the message to the best workflow. Supports `source_module` for module-scoped routing, `conversation_id` for multi-turn conversations, and `enabled_mcps` to control which MCP servers are active.

This is the recommended entry point for all client integrations.

item.name: Quality Feedback
item.description:
Quality feedback endpoint — submit ratings and comments on completed runs.

Allows clients to provide positive or negative feedback on agent run outputs. Valid ratings are 'positive' and 'negative'. Feedback is stored and used for quality monitoring.
